result.summary: Fix four edge cases in P2P opportunistic 1P1C package relay and orphan handling where transaction variants with identical txids can stall transaction propagation. Stop erasing orphan children upon reconsiderable package feerate failures, preserve txid requests for missing parents when a witnessless parent variant fails validation, track and request only actually missing parents instead of all transaction inputs, and stop inserting already-known transactions (TX_CONFLICT) into reject filters.
result.problem: Opportunistic 1P1C relay and orphan resolution query missing parents by txid, but cache validation failures and request states by wtxid. A peer providing a parent variant with the same txid but missing or modified witness data can poison reject filters, evict valid orphan children from the orphanage for all peers, or cancel in-flight parent download requests, delaying CPFP packages until the parent confirms or another peer announces it.
evidence: PR description: 'A peer sending a variant of a parent with the same txid and a different or missing witness could make the node drop the honest child, cancel the honest peer's request for the parent, or reject later children of that parent. Each case delays a CPFP package until a new announcer appears or the parent confirms.'

Commit 3b16af7e7a: 'Uniform random operations almost never reach the states where this matters, so bias the harness towards orphans with missing parents and towards TX_MISSING_INPUTS and TX_RECONSIDERABLE results. Without the bias, reverting the witnessless-parent fix survived 57k runs.'
result.scope_notes: Modifies validation to record and return missing parent txids on TX_MISSING_INPUTS failures, and updates both TxOrphanage and TxDownloadManager to handle these parents selectively.
result.changed_since_previous: Diff inspected; changes verified to include returning missing parents from validation PreChecks and corresponding unit, functional, and fuzz test additions.
result.card: This PR addresses four P2P opportunistic 1P1C relay and orphan handling vulnerabilities where a peer delivering an alternative parent variant (matching txid with altered or missing witness) can disrupt package relay. These bugs allow malicious or out-of-order peers to clear child transactions from the orphanage, cancel parent requests from honest announcers, or poison reject filters against confirmed or evicted transactions. The changes prevent these cross-peer cancellations and unblock invariant enforcement in PR #36371.

risk.why: Mistakes in transaction download and reject-filter management could stall mempool package relay or leak memory in the orphan and request pools.
